articleTitle: Literature survey on OPAL-RT Technologies with Advance features and Industrial applications
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: With the innovations of different computing technologies, several simulation tools have surfaced. They are the upgraded form of simulation tools with better performance capability and less cost. RT-LAB is an open real-time simulating software which is completely compatible with MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. The technology has completely revolutionized the performance of model based design. Because of its flexibility and scalability, this advance technology is implemented in many systems and control applications adding computing power to simulation at the time of need. Basically the real time simulator consists of tools such as real time distributed simulation package (RT-LAB) and algorithm tool boxes. While RT-LAB executes the simulink block diagram of PC-Cluster, the algorithmic tool boxes help in design of stiff electric circuits and their controllers. The real time simulation and Hardware in the loop (HIL) applications contribute a lot in different engineering designs such as Power electronics and electrical systems.

articleTitle: Assistant for Visually Impaired using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In this paper, a virtual assistant for the visually impaired is built using various technologies such as computer vision, object recognition, emotion detection, and text-to-speech using a micro-computer in order to describe the scene around as a narrative to the user. We generate an audio narrative by converting the scenes obtained by visual data in front of user to text which describes the important objects in the scene in audio format. Possible future ventures into involvement of various sensors to perform SLAM based navigation along with barcode reading.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement using grid interfaced PV with Multilevel inverter based hybrid filter
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In this paper, a Photovoltaic (PV) system integrated with Shunt hybrid active filter (SHAF) is coupled to three phase, four wire grid network. The proposed model uses a multilevel inverter configuration of three level H-bridge based Voltage source Inverter (VSI) for compensating load. Indirect current control technique is used for extraction of harmonics and calculating the reference current generation and found reliable performances related to conventional direct current control technique. For controlling the dc bus voltage, PI and fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is implemented. The operation of proposed system using conventional PI is compared with the FLC and is analysed in both direct and indirect current control technique. The proposed model is run and analysed using MATLAB/ SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: KHGI: Kinect-based Human Gait identification using Statistical Moments
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: As one of the biometric recognition systems, gait recognition aims to recognize the human gait style on-the-go when they walk. The Kinect sensor is a new camera originally designed for game play, which recently has been focused on by researchers, especially for gait based recognition methods. This study focuses on using Kinect sensor for extracting gait signatures to be used for gait recognition purposes. Moreover a new feature set is extracted by calculating Euclidean distance between each pair of 20 joint points, followed by the application of various statistical moments during one gait cycle, called the Euclidean Distance Feature (EDF). The extracted feature vector is a high dimensional feature set. Therefore, we need to decrease the dimensions of the feature set, hence we applied, Principal Component Analysis followed by Linear Discriminant Analysis. Finally, the Linear Discriminant Classifier (LDC) and Nearest Neighbors (NN) are used separately as classification methods. The results indicated that the proposed method achieves a significant result and provides a 92% recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Smart Car plate Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Smart car plate recognition System is addressed in this study. In particular, a graphical user interface using Matlab programming is used to recognize plates' numbers in order to deny or permit access to cars. The proposed interface acts as a first phase of a project to transform the main entrance of the facility to a fully automated car entrance control system by reducing the level of manned guarding at the main access points. This phase includes building a database of plates' numbers, creating the main processing interface, and simulate the controller as human aid system where a graphical user interface is used for processing and controlling car's entrance.

articleTitle: Comparison between the Optimal Sizing of a Photovoltaic System in Interconnected and Isolated Modes Using Gravitational Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Due to the widespread attention to renewable energy resources, including solar energy, Photovoltaic (PV) cells are becoming increasingly important and therefore, careful attention should be paid to their design and size. The main purpose of this study is comparison between the optimal size of PV systems in connected to the network mode and the isolated mode or separately operation, using gravitational search algorithm (GSA), and considering the economical and reliability constraints. For this purpose, problem formulation is divided to the separated and connected modes. The objective function is presented considering technical and economical constraints; and GSA is used for the optimization problem. The simulation results including the optimal sizing of the PV power plant as well as economical and reliability analysis are presented. The numerical results show that the optimal sizing in connected and isolated mode is 13 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 19 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: On Designing a Generic Framework for Big Data-as-a-Service
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Data is the heart of any system, which is perhaps the reason why big data is such a `big' deal. With the growing application domain of the technology, research towards big data analytical applications' development has gained immense attention lately. The cost-effective and scalable nature of Cloud Computing has made it an obvious infrastructural choice. However, until APIs are developed for provisioning analytical services, big data research will not meet its desired outcome. Moreover, existing frameworks are application-specific or cater to only a specific set of requirements. This paper proposes a framework for creating a technological stack for Big Data-as-a-Service. Besides this, it also presents criteria for technology selection, which is based on the identification of computing and data models for the application. Therefore, the proposed framework is application-independent and accommodates all the segments of the big data lifecycle.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Segmentation Using 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging Scans
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Designing automated systems for brain tumor extraction from a Medical Resonance Image is one of the most researched areas of the era. Automated systems will assist the doctors in automatic and early stage tumor detection which will allow doctors to spend more time on the treatment of the patient. This study uses marker controlled watershed segmentation to segment abnormally grown mass in brain, known as brain tumor, from an input 3D MR Image. 2D MRI give a restricted view of the brain, in this case, having a 3D image, will give a complete and comprehensive insight of any kinds of abnormalities residing inside the brain. The framework presented in this paper not only gives a thorough view of the brain, but also segments the tumor with great accuracy as depicted by the results.

articleTitle: High Speed 16×16 bit Booth Multiplier Based on Novel 4-2 Compressor Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In this paper implementation of a high speed 16×16 bit booth multiplier based on novel 4-2 compressor structure has been discussed. Starting from the design of 4-2 compressor a new structure has been proposed which is successively employed in the partial product reduction tree. Then by means of booth algorithm and with the help of previously reported works for high speed radix-4 booth encoding hardware implementation, the multiplier is implemented which can operate at the frequency of 350MHz. Simulation results for TSMC 0.18μm CMOS technology and 1.8V power supply using HSPICE depict the correct behavior of designed 4-2 compressor along the multiplier. The measured delay for critical path of proposed compressor is 255ps while the corresponding power consumption at the operating frequency of 1MHZ is 1.215μW.

articleTitle: Effects of Facial Mood Expressions on Face Biometric Recognition System’s Reliability
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Facial changes due to the user's emotional condition or facial mood expressions can affect the reliability of facial recognition system. Emotionally expressive faces can be typically classified by seven classes which are angry, disgusted, fearful faces, happy, normal, sad and surprised ones. In this paper we have presented one by one comparison between all samples from different moods in order to answer the following questions: 1- if the difference between samples matching score with different emotional facial expressions is statically significant? (Which mood can put the reliability of system in risk more than other ones?) 2- For each mood, what are the best and worst comparison scenarios from the biometric system's perspective? In order to answer the first and second questions, images with different expressions from Jaffe Database have been used. For calculation of matching scores, two state of the art methods, the face recognition dlib -deep cnn based - code and commercial code -Verilook- have been implemented. The obtained results showed in comparison with neutral faces, the mood influenced pictures can lead a statistically significant change in matching score. We have also reported that, for each mood which mood can be the least and most probable error source.

articleTitle: A Combination of C and U Double Negative Metamaterial having Negative Permittivity and Permeability at 28GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: The layout of this research work is to simulate a novel combination of C and U-shape unit cell at resonance frequency of 28 GHz for 5G operation, having negative permittivity and permeability which is often referred to as double negative metamaterial (DNG) or left-handed material. The DNG shape includes C and U resonators on one side of dielectric medium and a wire on other side. The Scattering parameters as well as permittivity, permeability and refractive index are determined from the simulated Simulations of DNG structure using Computer simulation technology (CST) in microwave studio (MWS). For verification of negative values of structure's parameter, MATLAB was used. This is a novel and promising design approach in the world of electromagnetics due to its simplicity, scalability and characteristics of double-negative material.

articleTitle: A Survey on Fuzzy Trust Management in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: The cloud computing concepts in last decade unexpectedly changed human's life with considerable features to convert the traditional computing to the ubiquitous one. For each untrustworthy technology like cloud, needing a great Infrastructure for Defense in confront of malicious attack is crucial subject.This paper describes some features of cloud, like service model, type of deployment model (Private, Community, Public, Hybrid), type of trust management used in the cloud and an overview of the proposed model for fuzzy trust systems helping the trust system to have more accuracy.

articleTitle: K.S.A Feed in Tariff
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Feed-in tariffs (FITs) are the greatest commonly used strategy in the globe for rushing renewable energy (RE) implementation, accounting for a better portion of RE enlargement than whichever tax motivations or renewable portfolio standard (RPS) strategies. FIT strategies classically contain three key supplies: (1) certain admission to the grid; (2) constant, continuing acquisition contracts (usually, about 10-20 years); and (3) imbursement levels founded on the prices of RE production. In nations such as Germany, they contain efficient administrative procedures that can help reduce lead stages, reduce managerial above, minimize scheme fees, and hurry the speed of RE assignment. Several European countries have enthusiastic to using FIT strategies to accomplish their long-term RE objectives out 2010 to and outside 2020, which specifies a long-term responsibility. In accumulation, European strategies typically spread suitability to everyone with the aptitude to capitalize, counting but not incomplete to proprietors, commercial proprietors and local government organizations. As this paper establishes, FIT strategy assemblies can differ extensively among authorities, reproducing a broad range of strategy purposes, which has an ability aptitude for adjusting to specific positions - and adopt specific strategy objectives is a significant component in the achievement of FIT strategies. Their ongoing achievement at development prompt RE development is likely to remain to fuel attention in these strategies universal.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Offset, its Distribution and its Impact on Multicarrier Spread Spectrum Techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Multi carrier is the utmost technology before preceding towards 5G. Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) is a basic spreading technique. Multi Tone CDMA (MT-CDMA), Multi Carrier CDMA (MC-CDMA), and Multi Carrier Direct Sequence CDMA (MC-DS-CDMA) are three types of Multi Carrier Spread Spectrum (MCSS). Carrier frequency offset (CFO) is one of the factors, which give birth to MAI and ICI. These interferences deteriorate the Spectral Efficiency(SE) of the network. Interesting fact is CFO among the subcarriers, spectral efficiency will increase with increase in the CFO. In this paper, we have compared two distributions of CFO "truncated-Gaussian, and uniform ". There is a significant increase in the performance of MCSS with increase in the variance of CFO. Another interesting fact, spectral efficiency also increases with increase in the SINR and number of interferers. Conclusively uniform Probability Density Function (PDF) of CFO outperforms truncated Gaussian PDF of CFO in all the three cases.

articleTitle: Online Partial Discharge Localization in Branched MV Joint
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Single and double side measurement methods have been reported for partial discharge source localization during online partial discharge (PD) measurements in medium voltage networks. However, these methods cannot be applied directly in branched networks due to the presence of multiple reflection points. The PD current pulses propagate simultaneously in the core and the earth screen of the cables with opposite polarities. Such pulses are negative during the positive half of the voltage cycle and vice versa. This paper studies the partial discharge source localization in branched networks by applying the direction of arrival of the pulses and peak pulse magnitude concept when HFCT sensors are used during the online PD measurements. The PD pulses tend to travel away from the discharge source and this property is utilized to identify the defective branch in a tee joints by tracing the PD pulses during their propagation. Lab studies of the pulse propagation were performed using online PD measurement systems, and the results are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Unified Protection Scheme For Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Recent advancements in renewable energy technologies have brought focus on microgrids that have resulted in many predicaments for safe and reliable operation. Two of the major protection concerns are varying fault level and island handling. Integration of various types of sources at different levels of power system alters the existing power system studies and jeopardizes the passive and radial nature of conventional systems. Connection and disconnection of utility grid and other power sources varies the fault levels of the system. Moreover, disconnection of main utility grid results in islanded mode operation where frequency and voltage can be unregulated. The concept of unified protection scheme for microgrid is proposed to meet the protection requirements, which comprises of a unified protection controller (UPC) that supervises the connection and disconnection of existing power sources and updates the relay settings accordingly. The proposed unified protection methodology has been analyzed in MATLAB Simulink. Faults are introduced in the system to check the capabilities of UPC in allowing correct tripping, preventing nuisance tripping.

articleTitle: A Novel Design and Analysis of C-Shaped Thickness of Metamaterial for Multi-Band Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel analysis of a C-shaped thickness of metamaterial unit cell structure that is applicable in a multi-band frequency range, which exhibits negative permeability and permittivity in those frequency bands. In the basic design, the separate rectangular resonator is inserted into a bigger split-resonator in a form of C-shape at a gap of 20mm to form a unit structure. Analysis and a comparison of the thickness of 0.1mm, 0.5mm, 1mm, 1.5mm and 2mm unit cell configurations were performed. These configurations demonstrate multi-band operational frequencies with double-negative characteristics. Equivalent circuit model and measured result for each unit cell validate the resonant behaviour. Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio, was used to obtain the reflection and transmission parameters of each unit cell. This is a unique and promising invention in the electromagnetic model for its double-negative characteristics, simplicity and multi-band operation.

articleTitle: Self-sufficient solar-based energy assessment in future cities – a preliminary study in the Sub-Sunbelt region
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Future smart cities metrics have complex and interdisciplinary targets. Energy portfolio and the ratio of self-consumption / sufficiency are key performance indexes for city long-term sustainability. Targeting 100% renewables production for mitigating climate change threats ask also for challenging solutions. As Europe is not enjoying the Sunbelt climate but still showed clear commitment towards high renewables penetration, the paper addresses the feasibility of a scenario targeting electrical energy production with 100% renewables and complete self-sufficiency in the so called Sub-Sunbelt region. A preliminary study, for specific cities in the Sub-Sunbelt region, is analyzed in terms of key performance indexes related to renewables production and self-sufficiency. For this, selected cities from the Sub-Sunbelt region (from 35° to 50° latitude north) in Greece, Spain, Romania and Austria have been chosen, by also making a comparison with sunny Sunbelt based cities Rabat and Dubai. The study suggests that high or complete self-sufficiency with solar based renewables is possible in Sub-Sunbelt regions, and that important renewables-based H2/CH4 long-term storage and consumption resources are also needed, while the Sunbelt regions can become exporters of renewables-based H2/CH4 by using their surplus energy during the summer time.

articleTitle: Determination of the Percentage of Participation of Free Users in the Peruvian Wholesale Electricity Market through an Multi-objective Optimization Model Based on Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Due to the evolution of the Wholesale Electricity Market that has arisen in Peru since the 1992 reform to the present, it has been demonstrated that the participation of the demand, and especially the Free Users, is a relevant factor that influences on the operation cost of the national electric system. It is for this reason that its regulatory process must be carried out through an optimization process that provides a market signal that leads to the economic benefit of the country.For these purposes, a methodology has been designed that calculates the percentage of participation of free users in the Wholesale Electricity Market, based on a Multi-objective Optimization Process, solved through the Nash Negotiation Model. With the results obtained, the entities competent to the regulatory and regulatory framework will have a quantitative tool to determine the degree of participation of Free Users in the Wholesale Electricity Market.

articleTitle: Frequency Response Analysis of Medium Voltage Distribution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: This paper describes the effects of some external faults on the frequency response analysis (FRA) signatures of medium voltage distribution transformer. Due to practical limitations, the laboratory experiments were limited to the external faults only. In addition, some computer simulation studies were also carried out using a transformer model reported in the literature to examine the frequency response analysis (FRA) signatures for a few selected cases. This paper shows that FRA signatures of experimental results as well as simulations are in reasonable agreement with each other. The obtained results can be helpful for engineers and researchers for further research in diagnosing the faults using the FRA method.

articleTitle: MEMS type hot cathode ion gauge
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of MEMS-type hot cathode ionization gauge is presented. The design is 2.4mm×0.8mm×1.4mm and can be fabricated with MMES technology. The design can measure in the HV and UHV range up to 10-9 torr vacuum. In this paper, various types of cathode creation methods are considered, and the preferred type is chosen as the proposed scheme. The cathode design is in a way that the temperature is uniform throughout it and remains almost constant with the vacuum pressure change. Simulation of CPT of COMSOL was performed to simulate the ionization process, and the sensitivity coefficient was obtained by simulation method. The simulation results in this design show the sensitivity factor of 0.6.

articleTitle: Novel Controller Design for High Order Transfer Functions Based on Similar Systems Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: This paper presents a new reduction method for systems with high order transfer functions. This new technique is essentially based on the nature of the three most common output responses with no overshoot, with overshoot only or with overshoot and oscillations. The approach is based on the concept of two similar systems but not identical. This similarity is made on significant weighted elements that characterize the real system. The controller will be designed based on the simple projected similar system and applied to the real or higher order systems. The characteristic of this new reduction method is that every system can be reduced to a similar first order system with same identified significant weighted elements that will be clearly defined. The merit of this new reduction technique is to avoid all mathematical equations to model the complex system and also to avoid huge mathematical equations to reduce its transfer function to an identical reduced system. The performance of the new reduction method was evaluated and compared with some reduction methods taken from the literature.

articleTitle: Optimization of Database Resources Assignment in Cloud Computing Using Gravity Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Cloud computing of the computational model is based on the great computer networks such as the internet; these networks propose a new pattern for providing, consuming, and delivering the Information Technology (including hardware, software, information, and the other common computational resources) by using internet. Cloud computing suggests guidelines to provide Information Technology services in similar ways such as public industries (water, electricity, telephone, etc.). This means that access to Information Technology at the time of demand and based on the user's demand level is provided for the users in a flexible and scalable way. On the other hand, the optimal resources in the cloud computing systems are considered from the fundamental challenges. Due to its large search space, this issue is from the difficult issues and the random search methods are more used for solving it. So far, different algorithms have been proposed for solving this problem. In this paper, for solving the resource assignment problem in cloud computing, we have used a meta-heuristic algorithm called GSA-RACloud. To show the performance of the proposed algorithm (GSA-RACloud), this algorithm has been compared with the ant colony algorithm (ACO). The empirical results show that the proposed algorithm has a higher performance than the compared algorithm.

articleTitle: A Decentralized Smart Distribution Management System
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: This paper proposes load management in an is-landed distribution network using Decentralized Multi Agent System (MAS) during contingency. The major grid features Sustainability, Energy Security, Reliability etc. became the challenges of the 21st century grid management due to the rapid proliferation of Distributed Renewable Generation (DGs) and the increasing number of Electrical Vehicles in to the grid. To manage the grid during a contingency alternate options are explored for the management of critical loads by using a hybrid model on integrating the DGs and Electric Vehicles (EVS) in a decentralized operation. Most critical loads have been prioritized and accordingly formulated the restoration strategy. The power restoration is formulated as a multi objective optimization problem considering maximization of the prioritized critical loads for restoration and minimization of switching operation subject to the constraints as power quality parameters. Developed the Software used to achieve the distributed Intelligence in the Distribution Network. The advantages and disadvantages for the V2G integration were assessed.

Author Keywords: FIPA- Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agencies

articleTitle: Mobility Management in SDN and NFV-based Next-Generation Wireless Networks: An Overview and Qualitative Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: The majority of contemporary 5G networks employ HetNets which improve data rate and the number of serving users over previous cell architecture. HetNets are comprised of different small-cell types such as femtocells and microcells. The tradeoff of these smaller cells is that they do not meet QoS requirements for flexibility and low latency because the increased frequency of handoffs increases network delay. This paper compares the state- of-the-art mobility management approaches that use SDN and (or) NFV concepts in 5G cellular networks. These approaches are evaluated in terms of scalability, signaling cost, probability of handoff failures, and system load balance.

articleTitle: A Comparative Review of Fault Location/Identification Methods in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Power failures are more frequent in Distribution Networks (DNs) compared to other sections of power system (generation and transmission). These failures are happened due to the occurrence of fault in the connected equipment or network. Consequently, the connected loads at consumer ends are affected until the service is restored. The time taken to restore the power or service back to the consumer may vary with the utilities based on the network complexity, design, availability of Fault Indicators (FI), etc. To improve the quality of restoring the service to the consumers, a faster service restoration technique needs to be adopted. The main challenge for the restoration process is the fault identification. Once the fault is identified, the service can be restored to the consumer within short time after proper isolation of the faulty section from the healthy portion of the network. In this paper, a comparative review of fault location/identification methods in DNs is carried out along with future research scopes in this area.

articleTitle: RoboCop; A Robust Surveillance Robot
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: This research paper discusses a surveillance robot Robocop that is controlled through a webpage and can be accessed remotely. Robocop is a kind of a surveillance robot which has been designed to capture and monitor the environment by providing live video streaming which eliminates the need of a human after being thrown at a place and is able to cover rough terrains as well. It is robust enough to bear stresses while being thrown at a place and not break and will have the ability to stable itself when landed in wrong orientation. In areas where it is difficult for humans to go or where the life of humans can be in danger (like the places containing explosive things or harmful gases) Robocop can be used in such environments. The main controller of this robot is Raspberry Pi 3B+ which will be the brain of this robot. The whole system is programmed on Raspberry Pi which will communicate with the webpage controller and make the robot work. The orientation of the robot will be decided by the tilt switch used in the robot which will make the robot move in the correct direction based on the command sent to it. The communication medium used in this robot is Wi-Fi which will receive and send signals. The Ultrasonic sensors are used for obstacle avoidance when the robot will run on autonomous mode otherwise it can be controlled through the webpage. Through testing we found that Robocop is able to bear the pay load of about 12 KGs. Such surveillance robots has a wide range of applications and can be used in the field of army, human rescuing and for the civilian security as well.

articleTitle: Tracking Indoor Elderly-People Using Onboard Smartphones Wi-Fi Device and Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In indoor/outdoor environments, special cares need to be given to elderly people. Tracking is valuable for those people who are in dangerous falling-situations inside the buildings. This tracking system needs a new positioning mechanism to offer very accurate services to the special needy people. To this end, this paper presents a mechanism to track elderly people using smartphones, specifically when they are indoors. The proposed mechanism incorporates onboard Wi-Fi and sensor devices including gyroscopes and accelerometers to provide accurate indoor smart phone positioning. This paper proposes an integrated approach to offer indoor smartphone positioning using. The purpose of the integrated approach is to fuse multi-technologies measurements on smartphones. The mechanism uses proximity-level (based on received-signal-strength `RSS' measurement) technique between the smartphone and Wi-Fi access-points. Then it combines this proximity measurement with uncertainty calculations from onboard dead-reckoning measurements using Extended-Kalman Filter, which can provide seamless, low cost, and improve location accuracy significantly, especially when deep indoor. This means, in deep indoor, the approach can utilize only a single WAPs signals as well as using prior-estimate positions based on artificial conditions. The results from different trial experiments (using Android-based smartphones) show that around 2.5-meters positioning accuracy can be obtained.

articleTitle: Kinect-based Human Gait Recognition using Triangular Gird Feature
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Gait recognition is a behavioral biometric system that has attracted a great deal of interest on the part of researchers recently. Several technologies such as CCTV camera and Kinect sensors have been used to recognize or to identify persons via their behavioral activities. However, using different image processing techniques and selecting various features to achieve high accuracy remains a challenge. This paper focuses on using a Kinect sensor for extracting gait signatures to be used for the process of gait identification. A set of triangles are created based on 20 joint points, which are provided by Kinect sensor. The uniqueness of this paper is the extracted feature based on the generated triangles using the triangle area and the three angles of each triangle, entitled the triangular grid feature (TGF). Furthermore, the extracted feature vector is a high dimensional feature set. Therefore, to reduce the dimensions of the feature vector, principal component analysis (PCA) followed by linear discriminant analysis (LDA) are applied as dimension reduction methods. Finally, Linear Discriminant Classifier (LDC) and k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) are used separately to test the performance of the proposed methods. The results obtained from the set of experiments shows that the proposed method achieves a significant result, and provides 90% and 87.3% in terms of recognition accuracy using k-NN and LDC, respectively.

articleTitle: LMI approach in Stability improvement through reactive power control in DG based hybrid power system
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Present research paper focuses reactive power management & voltage instability issues of a wind energy based dispersed power generating station. The iterative performances of PID controller as well as the robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> damping controller of the hybrid power system is designed through linear matrix inequalities (LMI) approach. The stability aspects of dispersed wind energy based HPS are considered for discussion where the issue of reactive power compensation is addressed by linear static var compensator (SVC) controller. The control aspects of SVC as well as the whole hybrid system are taken care by H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> linear matrix inequalities approach. The iterative LMI method has been implemented for tuning the gains of PID controller with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> design by the help of iterative LMI. The wind-diesel hybrid system is also implemented experimentally where a proto type hardware model has been established by taking the help of dSPACE real time control environment. In this case dSPACE 1104 is added for data acquisition and control. Experimental results obtained during practical case analysis justify the simulation results of MATLAB. Adaptability and robustness of the proposed controllers are achieved under fluctuating loads and wind power uncertainty.

articleTitle: Introducing a Fuzzy Method for Mapping Processes with Communications in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: In a parallel application which is divided into several tasks, choosing the right resource and sending tasks to the resources is an important challenge. Selecting the resources for each task in a way that the execution time of the application and usage of resources be appropriate is known as mapping tasks to the resources. In this paper, mapping and scheduling parallel applications, which have communications between their tasks, is investigated in the cloud environment. Our proposed method tries to reduce the execution time and also resource usage time by utilizing the fuzzy logic and reducing the communication overhead. In the end, the proposed method is compared with Max-Min-C and Min-Min-C algorithms, and results show a significant improvement.

articleTitle: Research on the Credible Capacity Model and Calculation Method of Photovoltaic Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 1st International Conference on Advanced Research in Engineering Sciences (ARES)
abstract: Due to the randomness and intermittency of solar energy, photovoltaic power plants can not express actual capacity with rated output. In the power system planning, we need to evaluate the contribution of PV grid connected to the reliability of the whole system, so it is necessary to study the credible capacity of PV generation. This paper presenting an algorithm of PV credible capacity based on sequence operation theory. By referring to the analysis process of wind power credible capacity, this paper deduces an analytical model of PV credible capacity. Taking advantage of RTS-79 system, this paper analyzes several factors that can affect PV credible capacity, getting the law how this factors including the capacity of PV power, the season and the geographical position affects the PV credible capacity.
